1 · Intent

find out if drag-to-reorder feels right before speccing a list editor

Does pointer-driven reorder feel good enough to build a real list editor around — and what's the persistence shape once a row moves?

2 · What I built / tried / worked / didn't

Keep it rough. This is the discovery log — the value is the learning, not the prose.

Built

  • A single-file demo list of 8 rows with pointer-driven drag-to-reorder and optimistic localStorage persistence.

Tried

  • The HTML5 drag-and-drop API first — ghost image + dragover bookkeeping felt janky.
  • Switched to raw pointer events with a transform on the dragged row.

Worked

  • Pointer-events reorder is smooth; the order persists across a reload via localStorage.
  • Reordering is optimistic — the row moves on pointermove, no round-trip.

Didn't

  • Touch devices need a long-press to start a drag, or the list just scrolls — unsolved here, an edge case for the spec.

3 · What actually ran

The commands you ran and what they proved. Captured in the verify.html Run/Demo shape so a later graduation can promote these facts to grounding="verified" with no re-capture.

pnpm --filter @demo/sortable-list dev none open http://localhost:5173, drag a row to reorder; the order persists across a full reload
